references.text: The same description of the kidneys and fat to be removed from the peace offering of small livestock, with identical wording regarding the kidneys, the fat on them near the loins, and the large lobe of the liver.
Parallel text concerning the kidneys and fat to be removed from the goat's peace offering, with the same anatomical details about the liver lobe and kidneys.
The same instructions are repeated for the sin offering of the bull—the kidneys with the fat near the loins and the liver lobe must be removed.
Identical wording in connection with the guilt offering regarding the two kidneys, the fat on them, and the liver lobe.
At the consecration of Aaron and his sons, mention is made of the fat covering the entrails, the large lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat.
In connection with the ram of consecration, mention is made of the fat, the tail, the fat on the entrails, the liver lobe, and the two kidneys.
It specifies how the law concerning fat and the kidneys in Lev 3 was practiced during the ordination of the priests.
It highlights that the requirement to remove all fat applies equally to communal offerings as it does to individual peace offerings.
It demonstrates the first practical fulfillment of the sacrificial laws regarding fat and kidneys after the ordination of the priests.
It illustrates how the law concerning fat and kidneys was practiced by Moses during the ordination of the priests.
